messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: PrivateLink reachability alert — us-west-2 AZ-b. Affected: customer AcmeCorp (ingress via VPC peering). High error rate on L7 TLS handshakes and DNS mismatch detected. Auto-escalate to #incidents and on-call.
alice.sre: I’m on it. seeing increased 5xx from the private endpoint healthchecks. correlating with route updates around 2412345000.
bob.netops: digging — BGP flaps reported between our peering and cloud provider in AZ-b. possibility of stale VIP being advertised from another AZ via leaked peering route.
carol-eng: Customer reports TLS cert CN mismatch and intermittent connection resets. likely resolving to wrong VIP (internal load balancer in AZ-c?)
tom-oncall: acknowledging pager — taking lead. @alice.sre please paste dig/traceroute outputs and any recent config changes.
alice.sre: dig +short acme-privatelink.redwood-internal
```
10.10.43.12
10.10.43.12
```
alice.sre: traceroute to 10.10.43.12 from host-worker-7:
```
1  10.10.1.1  0.6 ms
2  10.10.20.3  1.2 ms
3  192.0.2.45  12 ms  <-- unexpected hop to AZ-c transit
4  10.10.43.12  14 ms
```
alice.sre: note the path goes through 192.0.2.45 which is our peering path to AZ-c, not AZ-b.
bob.netops: confirmed on infra side — our route tables in VPC-peering for AcmeCorp leaked a /32 from AZ-c after an automated failover. cloud provider sent a withdrawal then re-advertised multiple times.
carol-eng: reproducing TLS error locally — SNI is `acme.app` but cert returned for `acme-int-azc.redwood`.
support-lead: customer impact: API calls to private endpoint failing for ~35% of requests for AcmeCorp in us-west-2. They opened a ticket and are looping in their networking team. We should give ETA for mitigation.
tom-oncall: immediate mitigation options:
  1) withdraw leaked route at peering (requires provider coordination) — best fix
  2) change AcmeCorp DNS to point to per-AZ fallback IP (temporary) — requires TTL change and customer approval
  3) apply connection-level proxy that forces correct backend selection — heavier ops work
any volunteers to attempt quick DNS TTL reduction and coordinated provider support?
alice.sre: I can submit a route withdraw with the provider now and open a support case. preparing diagnostic bundle.
eng-ops-bot: Automated change detected in route-manager at 2412344992: policy `failover-az` applied to AcmeCorp peering with prefer=az-c. Rolling back to prefer=az-b suggested.
bob.netops: If we roll back policy, we should be careful — previous change was intended to mitigate capacity in az-b. Need to confirm capacity first.
carol-eng: quick check of host health in az-b: service capacity at 78% CPU, ephemeral queue depth normal. I think rolling back is safe for short window.
alice.sre: Submitted case to provider (case#PROV-98721) asking for immediate withdraw of 192.0.2.45 announcement. ETA 15-20m.
alice.sre: Also changing internal DNS TTL from 300 -> 30 for acme-privatelink.redwood-internal to speed failover. pushing change now.
```
# nsupdate batch
server 10.0.0.2
zone redwood-internal
update delete acme-privatelink.redwood-internal A
update add acme-privatelink.redwood-internal 30 A 10.10.43.12
send
```
carol-eng: rolling config rollback on route-manager to remove `prefer=az-c` flag for AcmeCorp. plan: apply, monitor 5m, then provider withdraw should align.
eng-ops-bot: Route-manager change scheduled: rollback prefer flag at 2412345710 by carol-eng.
tom-oncall: good. @bob.netops please monitor for BGP flap reappearance and prepare to blackhole if we see route re-adverts causing cross-az churn.
bob.netops: watching. setup bgp-mon subscriptions and will pre-stage blackhole for 192.0.2.45 if it reappears.
```
# bgp-mon watch output
prefix 192.0.2.45/32 seen: 12 times in last 10m
state: flap -> pending-withdraw
```
support-lead: messaging AcmeCorp support: letting them know we're working on mitigation: route rollback + provider withdraw + DNS TTL reduction. providing Cx impact and ETA.
support-lead: "We are actively mitigating a PrivateLink routing issue that is causing some traffic to land in the wrong AZ, which manifests as TLS CN mismatches. We expect initial mitigation within ~20 minutes and full stabilization within 45 minutes."
alice.sre: provider just acknowledged case and applied withdraw at their edge — seeing withdrawal propagation now.
```
# bgp-routes dump (partial)
192.0.2.45       -> withdrawn
10.10.43.12/32   -> announced from us-west-2 AZ-b (preferred)
```
alice.sre: dig now returns correct VIPs across resolvers.
```
dig +short acme-privatelink.redwood-internal
10.10.43.12
```
carol-eng: TLS tests look clean now — cert CN matches `acme.app` and handshake times normalized.
tom-oncall: monitoring — set alert suppression for noise, but keep high priority for any reappearance. @bob.netops hold blackhole preparation until we see further re-advert.
bob.netops: blackhole pre-staged but not applied.
eng-ops-bot: change summary: route-manager rollback (id rm-3321) at 2412345710; DNS TTL change (id dns-881) at 2412345780; provider withdraw confirmed at 2412345855.
support-lead: informed AcmeCorp on stabilization. they will run their tests and confirm. asking for postmortem and RCA.
tom-oncall: shifting to watch mode. handing off incident to alice.sre for next 2h for verification and post-incident follow-up. I’ll mark oncall handoff.
alice.sre: taking over monitoring and postmortem lead. note to write RCA: include route-manager failover policy edge case that allowed cross-AZ advertise, TTL low-change timeline, and recommended guardrail: don't advertise AZ-specific /32 across peering.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> watch. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Incident owner: alice.sre. Pager history attached.
tom-oncall: thanks team — good response. will document timeline and action items in postmortems channel when I have a draft.
support-lead: action items captured:
  - Bob: add guardrail in route-manager to block cross-AZ /32 advertise across peering (due by EOD)
  - Carol: run capacity test in AZ-b and validate failover thresholds (due tomorrow)
  - Alice: RCA + customer timeline + provider case close (due 24h)
  - Tom: postmortem draft for ops review (due 48h)
alice.sre: ack. starting RCA notes now.
pagerbot: Page closed at 2412345930 — no active pages for this incident.
